newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end down, gold near new lows.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end down, gold near new lows.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower again Friday, with gold barely holding above its 20-month low posted Thursday.

"The partial recovery early this month enabled some funds to lighten up short positions, but everybody's back in now, with a target of $370 for spot gold," said Jeff Singer, Imperial Bank's chief dealer in California. "COMEX volume is up, open interest is up, and short term gold lease rates are up to 2.30 percent for one month, almost same as the 12 month rates, as suggesting there's heavy speculative shorting going on in the bullion market too."
"Gold's fundamentals have been bearish for long time and are probably already discounted into current prices, but things could really get interesting if $370 breaks," he said.
COMEX December gold closed down 20 cents at $376.30 an ounce, right on its session lows, but the new life-of-contract low at $375.80 set Thursday, was not breached Friday.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $376.10/376.60, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $377.00, and the New York close Thursday at $376.30/376.80.
COMEX December silver ended down 0.5 cent at $4.835 an ounce, after seeing a 12 day low at $4.805 Thursday.
Total estimated volume in COMEX gold futures Friday was a high 60,000 lots, after 77,372 lots were traded Thursday, while open interest rose 10,963 lots to 189,224 lots.
Estimated volume in COMEX silver Friday was 31,000 lots, after 44,062 were done Thursday, while silver open interest was up 980 lots.

"The focus is still on the December roll in gold and silver, with first delivery day next Wednesday, the OTC option expiry that day also, and the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday which will close the exchange for two days Thursday and Friday."

Gold has been under pressure this week from a sharp fall in the price of gold in Australian dollar terms and in South African rand, which encouraged some producer hedging from those countries, traders said.
Concerns about the potential for European central bank gold sales remain also, after a proposal to amend the Swiss constitution was reported Thursday.
The plan would remove the requirement that Switzerland hold gold reserves worth at least 40 pct of its currency in circulation, suggesting that country may have less need for gold.

But Switzerland already holds 83.3 million ounces of gold, more than sufficient to mee the 40 pct requirement, and had no need to remove the legal requirement if it wanted to sell gold, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down 50 cents at $386.80 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium closed down 80 cents at $118.60.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
